why: Narrowing the tub from 18 to 13 cm inner width brings it to 18 cm overall. With 0.41 cm steering sigma at slow duty, that leaves about 1.7 cm in the 19.7 cm opening. For the lawn the whole route needs about 5.24/0.78 = 6.7 Wh at 0.38 kg. Going to 12 Wh (5 NiMH cells, +81 g, about 0.46 kg) gives about 10.2 Wh usable against an estimated 7.5 to 8 Wh needed once the extra mass is counted. Both changes are free: 4 spare nimh_aa are on hand, and the tub is a reprint of 162 g of PLA, about 162 machine minutes. Neither needs a swap.

No parameter of bump_switch changes its 0 m range, so the part itself has to change. The HC-SR04 ranges 2 m in any light, adds no height and draws only 0.08 W. The robot can then cruise the 8 m corridor near its 0.94 m/s and steer around the obstacles instead of spending 4 s on each. The 11 m route should then take about 15 to 25 s. The camera would light only 0.12 m in the dark, and lidar is not provided. Cost: $2.50, 2 days.

No wheels4 size can fix these three. A wheel never climbs above its radius (4.5 cm max is less than 5.5 cm), and a 9 cm diameter is still under the 9.2 cm trench. Rocker-bogie with 6 cm wheels would stand about 14 cm tall and fail under_sofa's 9 cm overhang. Tracks: idler 6 cm should meet the 5.5 cm step, and the track stands 7.5 cm overall, under the 9 cm sofa. track_length 24 should bridge 0.45 x 24 = 10.8 cm, more than the 9.2 cm trench. Two 24 cm tracks give on the order of 100+ cm2 of contact, so at about 0.6-0.7 kg the pressure is about 0.5 kPa and sinkage under 1 cm, below the 2 cm belly. Last time's refusal was a track-to-tub length mismatch; tub length 24 now matches the 24 cm track. The 1.8 cm sprocket cuts top speed to about 0.56 m/s, so the lawn takes about 8,900 s (14,400 allowed). At that speed the electronics alone use about 6.4 Wh, plus a higher drive term from track rolling resistance. Three 18650 cells (28.2 Wh, 138 g, about the same mass as the current 5 NiMH cells) cover that. Width 10 also narrows the body for the bedroom door. Stall force with 2 motors on the small sprocket is about 16/2 x 3/1.8 = 13 N, still several times what the 22 deg ramp needs.

The ratio is 5.40/6.0 = 0.90, or equivalently an offset of 0.6 cm. Either way, an idler at 6.5 cm should meet edges up to about 5.85-5.9 cm, which clears the 5.48 cm step with about 0.4 cm to spare. Force is not the limit: stall force is 13.3 N, 2.27 times the robot's weight. A cheaper move isn't available because only idler_height sets the climbable edge, and the current part's range [2, 8] covers the fix, so no swap is needed. The cost is $0 and about 57 machine minutes to reprint the track frames (314 available). Overall height goes from 7.5 to 8.0 cm (idler + 1.5 cm).
